body:
Ready for review.

Quick pass on head def62da2:
- The PR merges cleanly with main.
- The quick gate is green on this head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, 0 failed.
- Pinning tests: `turning_hidden_floor` (5 tests) and `turned_hidden_rest` (4 tests). Each of the six excuses and guards was mutation-checked: deleted, the tests go RED; restored, they go GREEN. The table is in the body.

This is safety-floor work (the rest/gouge verdict), so the review should run at the effort:high tier.

<!-- pr-reviewer: def62da2223600917ca2d0667077e90197cc5802 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (safety floor: the new hidden-half excuse lets an under-cut groove post clean).

Thanks for the careful write-up and the mutation table. I trial-merged with current main (clean), and also ran extra probes of my own, local only, not pushed.

**What looks good**
- The change is scoped: without `lathe_axis` the scan is the old one (pinned bit for bit; `lathe_axis_of` returns `None` for every non-`Family::Turn` op and for a nose-less tool, and the plane-frame call site passes `None`). Gouge half and visible half are untouched.
- The orbit reading only ever over-reads (min over samples on the top's own orbit), the leave is only subtracted when a spindle is given, and non-finite input degrades to the old reading.
- No new dependency, no build.rs/.github/process-file change, no goldens or PNGs touched, provenance lines present, decision record included.

**Local results (merged with main)**
- `camcraft-sim` full test run: all ok. `turned_hidden_rest` 4/4, `hidden_rest_banded`, `midturn_*`, `ridge_*`, `scan_arc`, `boundary_arc_planes`, `model_excess` ok.
- `camcraft-app`: `turning_hidden_floor` 5/5; every `turning*` / `lathe*` suite plus `verify`, `turn_pivot`, `sim_lathe_body`: all ok.
- Pinning check: with the src change reverted, `turning_hidden_floor` gives 2 passed / 3 failed (the three "posts" tests); the two "still blocks / posts as before" guards pass either way, as intended. The sim tests need the new API, so they do not compile against the old src (they only prove the new behaviour).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

**Requested before merge**
1. The band excuse (`scan_turned.rs` `reaches`, used at `scan_hidden.rs` ~line 324) also excuses a groove the op entered but did not cut to the floor. Probe on the issue's groove bar (r10, groove r5.5 over z34..37, nose 0.8, tol 0.05, spindle Z, leave 0): a path that rides the OD down and then goes into the groove at centre z=34.8 to r=6.3 reads rest 0 (correct, floor cut); the same path with r=8.0 reads 1.122 (correct, radial shortfall convicts); but at centre z=35.5 (floor 0.7 below the nose bottom) with r=6.3 or r=8.0, and at z=36.0 with r=6.3, the scan reads 0.000 and the program would post. Those are real owed floors inside the pass's own groove, the exact thing a finish envelope exists to refuse; the band clause cannot tell "another op's floor" from "this op stopped short". Please narrow the excuse to a top the pass could not have been aimed at (for example only excuse a band-external top when no path station of the pass lies inside that top's own groove/recess width, or when the top is beyond the end of the part's last path), and add a test for the shallow-in-groove path above (convicts) next to the facing case (posts).
2. Add the shallow-groove case to `turning_hidden_floor.rs` through `post_script` (a profile finish whose path stops short of the floor), since law (f) is the only line that sees it (the groove floor is hidden, not a ridge).

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Stock left on a faced end or an OD (centre at z=49.5, or r=11.5) reads 0 with and without the spindle, on a plain bar on main too: pre-existing, not caused by this PR (the envelope law judges ridges and hidden floors; bulk stock is the stock sim's).
- `scan_hidden.rs` is at 357 lines, `scan.rs` 386: under the limit but near it.
- The "Not exercised" list in the body (boring/chamfer/taper/multi-pass with a groove, MCP repro not re-run) stands; nothing was stated as held. No GUI or machine hand check is owed by the body.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Back to draft for a review fix: the band excuse is being narrowed so a pass that went into a groove and stopped short of its floor no longer posts clean (review item on def62da). Commit and results follow in the next comment.

Review fix pushed: b851ef625 (on def62da).

**Rule chosen.** Being out of the nose's reach along the spindle does not prove a floor belongs to another operation, because every floor a pass stops short of is out of its reach. `TurnedBand` now also records each segment's station span. A hidden top is excused only when both of these hold:
- it is out of reach;
- no segment stands level (within the same reach) with its recess. The recess is the open span up the scan's Z from the top to the part's next surface over it, which is the groove's width at that radius.

A pass that went into the recess owns its floor. A floor under a facing, or a groove beyond a profile window, is still excused. The rule only narrows the old one: it still needs the old "out of reach" condition. Milling paths (no band) are unchanged. The excuse applies only to a spindle along Z. Any other spindle is judged without it, so it refuses and never passes. The decision file has the rule and the dropped alternatives.

**Probe (nose 0.8, groove r 5.5 over z 34..37, down the OD and into the groove at centre z, r)**

| z | r | rest before | rest after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34.8 | 6.3 | 0.000 | 0.000 (floor cut) |
| 34.8 | 8.0 | 1.122 | 1.122 |
| 35.5 | 6.3 | 0.000 | 0.695 |
| 35.5 | 8.0 | 0.000 | 1.502 |
| 36.0 | 6.3 | 0.000 | 1.194 |

**Tests added (both fail on def62da):**
- `turned_hidden_rest::a_pass_that_stops_short_of_the_groove_floor_it_entered_convicts` (sim): pins the table above.
- `turning_hidden_floor::a_finish_that_stops_short_of_the_groove_floor_is_refused` (app): a ProfileFinish stopping at z 35.5 on the groove bar carries an envelope warning and its post is blocked ("post blocked", "S1", "finish envelope"). Facing on the same bar still posts.
- Unit tests in `scan_turned`: a recess the pass stood in is never excused, a recess with no roof is never excused, and a spindle off Z is never excused.

**Gate:**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` for every turning*/lathe*/verify*/turn_pivot/sim_lathe_body suite: green, 842 passed and 0 failed across both runs.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed.

**Not exercised:**
- A turning spindle not along Z: it is now judged without the excuse (errs refusing). No fixture covers a groove on such a spindle.
- Boring, chamfer, taper and multi-pass profile programs on grooved parts.
- An MCP or CLI reproduction.
- A finish that rides over a groove mouth (path above the OD, level with the recess) now refuses where it passed before. This is deliberate, and no suite has such a case.

Ready for a re-review.

<!-- review-cost: b851ef625e9ea3cd50c01c406ef62ec617692775 -->
**Estimated agent cost to merge-ready:** ~$1.32 for the two known runs (236k tokens)
| Run | Model | Tokens | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| first review (needs-rework) | Sonnet 5.5 | not known | - |
| narrowed rule and tests (fix worker) | Opus 5.5 | 115k | ~$0.64 |
| re-review | Opus 5.5 | 121k | ~$0.68 |
Blended upper estimate (90 % input / 10 % output at list price; cache reads make the real cost lower). Main-session coordination isn't counted.
Effort: effort:high
